INTEGRATED GIMBAL PLATFORM / DESIGN SPECIFICATIONSPRELIMINARY DEVELOPMENT TARGETS

A premium motor.
A complete architecture.

A premium motor and power-electronics development program with onboard control, a protected power stage, and redundant feedback. The specifications below remain preliminary development targets.

12–30 V DCInput range · 24 V nominal
≈80 WElectrical input target
≥1 N·mTorque target
≥150 RPMSpeed target

Targets from the preliminary PCB architecture. Torque duration, simultaneous torque–speed capability, duty cycle, cooling, and environmental limits are not yet specified or validated. The <20 mm axial target is subject to confirmation for the complete integrated assembly.

Proposed integrated motor architecture
SubsystemProposed specificationIntegration considerations
Motor & packagingSlotless, direct-drive BLDC; ultra-low-profile architectureCustom windings, mounting, load interface, and thermal integration
Control modesField-oriented current control; torque, speed, and absolute-position controlKV-specific characterization and application tuning
Control-loop targetsCurrent: 20–40 kHz; speed: approximately 1–2 kHz; position: approximately 1 kHzFinal rates depend on controller, feedback, timing, and application requirements
Power switchingThree-phase inverter; proposed SiC MOSFET stage; 40–100 kHz switching studyDevice technology and frequency remain subject to efficiency, thermal, and EMC trade studies
Power regulation3.3 V logic; 5 V sensors; isolated gate-driver supplies; per-rail eFuse protectionReverse-polarity, surge, inrush, and fault monitoring provisions
Position feedbackAbsolute encoder with redundant channels; Hall sensingSPI, SSI, or BiSS-C interface selection; resolution and accuracy to be defined
Customer interfaceCAN FD commands, configuration, status, and diagnosticsPower and CAN connectors selected around packaging and environment
IsolationProposed galvanic separation of logic and power, with isolated control and CAN interfacesIsolation ratings and boundary implementation to be defined
Monitoring & protectionCurrent, bus voltage, and distributed temperature sensing; derating; hardware torque-disable pathRedundancy, shutdown behavior, and safety integrity require application-specific validation
Firmware & diagnosticsSecure boot, hardware watchdog, authenticated service access, event and fault loggingSecurity implementation and CAN command protocol remain in development
QUALIFICATION IS APPLICATION-SPECIFIC

Environmental and EMC planning includes evaluation against selected MIL-STD-810 and MIL-STD-461 requirements where applicable. Test methods, severity levels, power-quality requirements, and acceptance criteria will be agreed for each application. These are design objectives, not completed qualifications, radiation-hardness claims, or certified Safe Torque Off functionality.

MECHANICAL TARGETS & MATERIAL OPTIONS

<20 mm axial target

Confirm the complete stack including bearings, position feedback, onboard electronics, connectors, and load interface.

Ti-6Al-4V housing concept

Grade 5 titanium is under evaluation. Wall thickness, stiffness, mass, and thermal expansion require geometry-specific analysis.

Conduction cooling concept

Boron-nitride-filled potting with expanded graphite or OFHC copper interfaces to the customer’s structural heat sink.

Mechanical qualification plan

Application-specific validation of rotor retention, bearing loads, air-gap clearances, structural compliance, shock, and vibration.
